blocks.tamil_translation: Prophet ﷺ spoke to him gently. After he left, Hazrat Aishah (RA) asked, “Ya Rasulallah, you said (he is the worst among his people) and then spoke gently to him?” The Prophet ﷺ replied, “The one whom people stop associating with because of his evil words will be at the worst rank with Allah Ta'ala on the Day of Qiyamah.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- The Prophet ﷺ said words of censure about the man who was about to come only in order to make known the true state of that man and to protect people from his harm. Therefore this does not count as backbiting. Moreover, by speaking gently to the man who came, Rasulullah ﷺ taught how one should deal with such people; there is also a lesson in this on how he should be reformed.
(Mazahir-e-Haq)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: اَلْمُؤْمِنُ غِرٌّ كَرِيْمٌ، وَالْفَاجِرُ خَبٌّ لَئِيْمٌ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد، باب في حسن العشرة، رقم:٤٧٩٠
blocks.tamil_translation: “The (believer) is guileless and noble, whereas the sinner is a deceiver and base.” Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said this.

blocks.text: Explanation:- Scheming, trickery and the like are not the natural disposition of a Mu'min. Because of his naturally noble character, a Mu'min keeps away from causing hardship to people, thinking ill of them and the like. On the contrary,
